risk_rationale: The snapshot contains authentication, session, administrative, LLM/RAG, external-token, CI/CD, and production-deployment authority surfaces.
Missing Git and deployment context prevents change-level attribution and requires conservative treatment.

agent_permissions: Read-only inspection; no target writes or external validation
limitations: The supplied directory has no .git metadata, owner declaration, merge request, AI-assistance record, or attestation.

findings.title: Administrative and sensitive API operations lack application authorization
findings.entry_point: HTTP requests to mounted /v1 reporting, upload, document-management, document-job, session, and generation route groups
findings.source_to_sink: Routes are mounted without authentication or role middleware; handlers return conversation history or change vector-store and document-job state.
findings.trust_boundary: Unauthenticated client to application data and administrative operations
preconditions: The backend is reachable and no upstream gateway independently enforces equivalent authentication and authorization.

evidence.summary: Eleven /v1 route groups are mounted after session setup with no authentication or authorization middleware; sensitive handlers perform reads and state changes.

findings.impact: An unauthenticated caller can potentially read conversation records and manipulate uploaded knowledge, document state, or administrative jobs.
findings.exploitability: Direct at the application layer when reachable; upstream identity enforcement was not supplied and must be confirmed.
findings.false_positive_considerations: A separately configured API gateway could reduce external reachability, but no repository evidence demonstrates that control or per-operation authorization.
findings.recommendation: Require authenticated identities and server-side role or ownership checks at each sensitive operation; deny by default and independently test unauthorized roles.
verification: Static call-path review from route mounting to reporting and document mutation handlers
Confirm gateway configuration, then run authorized negative tests for anonymous, ordinary, and administrative roles
open_questions: Is every deployed route protected by an upstream identity-aware gateway?

findings.title: Unauthenticated callers can place and activate content used as LLM retrieval context
findings.entry_point: Unauthenticated PDF and image-context upload endpoints plus unauthenticated document activation
findings.source_to_sink: Caller-controlled content is embedded with caller-selected contentFor metadata, can be activated without authorization, is retrieved from active vector records, and is inserted into the model prompt context.
findings.trust_boundary: Untrusted uploaded content to trusted retrieval corpus and model-visible instructions
preconditions: The API is reachable, model and storage credentials are configured, and the caller selects a contentFor value used by an avatar.

evidence.summary: The upload, activation, retrieval, and prompt-formatting path is present without a corpus-write authorization or content-promotion gate.

findings.impact: A caller can poison the active knowledge base and influence model responses shown to users, undermining content integrity and potentially exposing retrieved information through crafted instructions.
findings.exploitability: The path is complete in source; successful operation also requires configured external services and database access.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Documents default to inactive, but the activation operation is also mounted without application authorization.
findings.recommendation: Restrict ingestion and activation to approved roles, separate upload from reviewed promotion, validate corpus provenance and integrity, and treat retrieved text strictly as data with injection-focused evaluations.
verification: In an isolated authorized environment, verify anonymous upload and activation are denied and seeded instruction-like content cannot alter system policy
open_questions: Is corpus approval enforced outside the repository?

findings.title: Provider session tokens can be minted without an application authorization check
findings.entry_point: POST request to the frontend server API token route
findings.source_to_sink: Caller-supplied avatar and voice identifiers are sent using a server-held provider key, and the returned provider session token is relayed to the caller without an authentication, authorization, or quota check.
findings.trust_boundary: Unauthenticated web client to privileged third-party provider credential and billable session capability
preconditions: The frontend API route is deployed and reachable and the provider key is configured.

evidence.summary: The POST handler calls the provider with the server-side key and returns the resulting session token without checking caller identity.

findings.impact: Unauthorized users can consume provider sessions, incur cost, exhaust quota, or use unapproved avatar and voice combinations.
findings.exploitability: Direct when the route is public; no source-level mitigating control was found.
findings.false_positive_considerations: An upstream authenticated proxy could limit reachability, but no evidence of that control was supplied.
findings.recommendation: Authenticate the caller, enforce server-side avatar and voice allowlists, apply per-user authorization and rate limits, and avoid returning provider error bodies verbatim.
verification: Test that anonymous and unauthorized requests are rejected before any provider call and that quotas are enforced
open_questions: Does the deployment platform apply route-level authentication before this handler?

findings.title: Deployment jobs execute unpinned remote code and promote mutable artifacts
findings.entry_point: Manual production and lower-environment GitLab deployment jobs
findings.source_to_sink: Jobs install an unpinned package, pipe a script from a mutable remote branch directly to a shell, and promote images identified by mutable latest tags before obtaining and using deployment credentials.
findings.trust_boundary: External package and source hosting to privileged CI runner and cloud deployment control plane
preconditions: A deployment job runs and the remote installer, package resolution, network path, or mutable image tag is compromised or unexpectedly changed.

evidence.summary: The production deployment path contains direct remote-script execution without digest or signature verification and uses mutable image references.

findings.impact: Compromised upstream content can execute in the deployment job, access CI material, alter downloaded credential files or artifacts, and affect production deployment.
findings.exploitability: Requires a deployment run and compromise or substitution of an unpinned input; the production jobs are manual but consequential.
findings.false_positive_considerations: HTTPS and manual approval reduce some risk but do not establish content integrity or immutable artifact identity.
findings.recommendation: Pin and verify the installer and Python packages, use approved immutable CI images, promote image digests rather than latest tags, and isolate credential acquisition after artifact verification.
verification: Confirm every deployment input resolves to an approved immutable digest or signed artifact and that production deploys the reviewed digest
open_questions: Is the remote installer mirrored or integrity-verified by runner controls outside this file?

findings.title: Session and JWT signing configuration accepts static fallback secrets
findings.entry_point: Application startup without required secret environment variables
findings.source_to_sink: Missing environment configuration silently selects repository-visible fallback literals for session and JWT signing.
findings.trust_boundary: Deployment configuration to authentication and session integrity controls
preconditions: A deployment omits the applicable secret environment variable.

evidence.summary: Both controls use environment values with fixed source-code fallbacks; raw fallback values were not reproduced in the pilot output.

findings.impact: A configuration mistake can make signing material predictable and weaken session or token integrity.
findings.exploitability: Depends on the environment variables being absent; the JWT verifier was not found on protected route paths, while the session secret is active.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Correctly configured environments avoid the fallback, but the application does not fail closed when configuration is missing.
findings.recommendation: Remove fallback literals, require high-entropy managed secrets at startup, fail fast when absent, and rotate any environment that used the fallback.
verification: Start in an isolated environment without each secret and verify startup fails without disclosing secret material
open_questions: Were any deployed environments started with the fallback configuration?

findings.title: Retrieved documents and conversational content are written to application logs
findings.entry_point: User questions, chat history, retrieved corpus records, and model responses
findings.source_to_sink: Application code logs standalone questions, retrieved document content and metadata, message history, and model answers at info or debug levels.
findings.trust_boundary: Application and model data to centralized operational logging
preconditions: The affected paths execute and the configured logger exports or retains the corresponding levels.

evidence.summary: Retrieved page content is logged at info level and conversational data is logged at multiple points.

findings.impact: Potentially confidential corpus content, user questions, session context, and model responses can be exposed to log readers and retained beyond application data policy.
findings.exploitability: Requires access to logs or a downstream logging service; actual data classification and logger configuration were not supplied.
findings.false_positive_considerations: If all content is public and logs are tightly controlled with suitable retention, impact is lower; that evidence was unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Log identifiers, counts, timing, and redacted metadata instead of content; define classification-aware retention and access controls.
verification: Exercise representative requests in an isolated environment and confirm logs contain no question, document, session, credential, or model-response content
open_questions: What data classification, retention period, and audience apply to production logs?

findings.title: Tier 3 security behaviors have no executable behavior-level test evidence
findings.entry_point: Repository test configuration and the only two discovered test files
findings.source_to_sink: No package defines a test command; the backend tests import an absent path and cover only welcome and not-found responses, leaving authentication, authorization, ingestion, RAG, provider-token, and CI security claims untested.
findings.trust_boundary: Security-sensitive implementation claims to release and approval evidence
preconditions: The supplied snapshot accurately represents the repository test configuration.

evidence.summary: Only two superficial backend tests were found, their import target is absent, and no test script is defined in any package manifest.

findings.impact: Security regressions in access control, corpus integrity, external token issuance, and sensitive-data handling can reach review without independent executable evidence.
findings.exploitability: This is an assurance gap rather than a direct attack path; it materially reduces confidence in Tier 3 controls.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Tests may exist in an external pipeline or omitted repository location, but no such evidence was supplied.
findings.recommendation: Add a deterministic test command and behavior-level negative, role, corpus-promotion, provider-token, logging, and regression tests with durable outcome assertions.
verification: Run the approved test command in isolation and demonstrate unauthorized cases fail while authorized cases pass
open_questions: Does a separate private test suite cover these behaviors?

checks_performed: adder-3pp-dependency-hygiene offline manifest and lockfile review
adder-threat-model split STRIDE and MAESTRO review
checks_not_performed: Live endpoint validation or exploit testing
Test execution or build: no test command is defined, the discovered backend tests reference an absent import target, dependencies were not installed, and the target remained read-only
Authoritative package existence, publisher, vulnerability, malware, maintenance, and reputation checks: no approved registry or intelligence access was supplied
Git diff and history review: the supplied snapshot contains no .git directory
Deployment, gateway, runtime, log-platform, cloud-IAM, and production configuration validation
required_actions: Add application-layer authentication and operation-specific authorization before reports, document management, ingestion, generation, and administrative job actions.
Separate RAG ingestion from reviewed activation and add provenance, integrity, and prompt-injection controls.
Protect provider-token issuance with identity, allowlists, rate limits, and quota controls.
Replace unpinned CI downloads and mutable image promotion with verified immutable artifacts.
Remove fallback signing secrets and minimize content logging.
Add executable behavior-level security tests and rerun ADDER against a Git-backed change with approved package intelligence.
required_approvals: Data owner for corpus, conversations, and logs
exception_path: No exception was supplied. Any exception must meet policies/core-decision-policy.md and cannot erase findings.
limitations: Static read-only review of a non-Git source snapshot; no network calls, package installation, credential validation, service startup, or production interaction occurred.
Reachability and severity assume no equivalent upstream identity or network control; deployment evidence is required to resolve that assumption.
The two database-string scanner candidates were environment-composed values rather than embedded credentials; raw values and secret material were not persisted in pilot artifacts.
